title: Private deployment compliance evidence and RBAC checklist
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the minimum RBAC model, audit logging expectations, data residency and retention controls, secure-SDLC gates, incident response evidence collection steps, and compliance-evidence packaging for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It targets Redwood Private customers and the internal teams (Solutions, SRE, Security, and Customer Success) responsible for onboarding and operating those deployments. The document is scoped to inference control plane and model-serving endpoints, admin consoles, and any data plane components that persist customer-provided prompt/response data.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all Private deployments managed by Redwood where customer data or keys are resident in customer-managed networks or air-gapped premises.
- Excludes pure-hosted API customers unless an explicit hybrid arrangement is documented.
- Covers: RBAC, audit logging (ingest, retention, redaction), data residency and retention policy mapping, SDLC deployment gates for private packages, incident response evidence collection, and exception handling for control plane access.

Principles and high-level SLOs:
- Principle: Least privilege by default for all entitlements.
- Principle: Immutable, tamper-evident audit trail for all privileged actions with cryptographic integrity where supported.
- SLO: Audit ingestion latency <= 30s for control-plane events (measured at 95th percentile).
- SLO: Audit-collection completeness >= 99.999% for actions that change entitlements or access controls over a rolling 30-day window.
- Retention baseline: 1 year for operational events, 7 years for legal/regulated evidence (configurable per contract and law).

Ownership and primary contacts:
- Onboarding lead: Solutions Eng (owner: aisha.patel@redwood.example)
- RBAC policy custodian: Platform Security (team alias: platform-security@redwood.example)
- Audit collector & retention: Eng SRE (alias: eng-sre@redwood.example)
- Evidence packaging & legal liaison: Security & Compliance (security-compliance@redwood.example)

RBAC model and checklist (private deployment specifics):
- Roles (recommended minimal set):
  1. deployment-admin — full control over deployment lifecycle, can create/rotate service identities and change network config.
  2. tenant-admin — customer-designated role for per-tenant config (model pinning, usage quotas, data retention overrides).
  3. operator — runtime ops for scaling/backups; cannot change entitlements or customer mappings.
  4. observer-audit — read-only access to logs, metrics, and evidence bundles; no ability to read plaintext customer content.
  5. emergency-signer — timebound JIT role for escalations; must be activated via approval flow and is automatically revoked.

- Checklist for RBAC enforcement in private deployments:
  - All human access must be mapped to SSO identities and short-lived sessions (OIDC/SAML).
  - Service accounts must follow a naming convention: svc/<team>/<purpose>/<deployment-id>.
  - No long-lived credentials stored in plaintext on nodes; require KMS/HSM-backed secrets.
  - JIT access flow: activate emergency-signer with MFA, ticket ID, and 2 approvers. Activation window <= 4 hours and audited.
  - Periodic certification: quarterly entitlement review with evidence exported to evidence-bucket (see Compliance Evidence Workflow).

Audit logging and evidence requirements:
- Events to capture (minimum):
  - Authn events: successful/failed logins, MFA challenge results, token issuance/refresh.
  - Authorization events: allow/deny decisions for admin and tenant-admin APIs.
  - Entitlement changes: role grants/revocations, policy updates, JIT activations.
  - Deployment actions: image rollouts, config changes, network policy updates, inbound firewall changes.
  - Data-access alerts: retrievals of persisted customer content flagged as sensitive.

- Required event fields (flat JSON schema snippet shown as example only):
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-01-15T12:34:56Z",
    "event_id": "uuid-v4",
    "actor_id": "user:alice@customer.example",
    "actor_type": "human|service",
    "action": "role.grant",
    "target": "role:tenant-admin",
    "deployment_id": "priv-deploy-123",
    "request_id": "req-xyz",
    "outcome": "success|failure",
    "metadata": "(string blob for low-sensitivity additional context)"
  }

  Note: The snippet above is to be emitted as a single-line JSON event to the configured audit sink. Do NOT include customer PII or raw prompts in the top-level event payload; instead include references (blob IDs) that point to encrypted storage.

- Redaction and sensitivity classification:
  - All prompt/response content marked as Sensitive must be hashed and stored in encrypted blobs with access restricted to tenant-admin only.
  - Audit events MUST NOT include plaintext prompt content.
  - Where plaintext is required for debugging under a legal hold, follow the Legal Hold workflow (see Data Residency & Retention).

Data residency, retention, and legal hold:
- Mapping table (textual representation):
  | Data class | Default residency | Default retention | Legal hold behavior |
  |-----------|------------------:|------------------:|---------------------|
  | Operational logs (non-customer) | Redwood control plane region | 1 year | retained until release |
  | Customer prompts/outputs (sensitive) | Customer VPC / on-prem storage | contract-defined default (30–365 days) | frozen, encrypted, access logged |
  | Audit trail (system events) | Customer-controlled bucket where required; else Redwood immutable store | 1 year operational; extendable to 7+ years | preserved and exported to legal archive |

- Legal hold process (abridged):
  1. Legal issues request hold via security-compliance ticket with case number.
  2. SRE marks related data blobs as immutable and moves to the hold storage class.
  3. All access requires documented justification; access requests are logged and added to the evidence manifest.

Secure SDLC gates for private packages and images:
- Pre-release checks (must pass before image can be signed):
  - Static analysis (SAST) and dependency SBOM verification.
  - Container image vulnerability scan (critical CVEs must be remediated or exception documented).
  - Secrets scan: no embedded keys, verified by pipeline verifier.
  - RBAC policy change tests: unit/integ tests that assert no wildcard grants for tenant namespaces.
  - Signed-by: Build must be signed by the CI pipeline key; signature captured in release evidence.

- Release evidence bundle (per private package):
  - Build artifact SHA256, SBOM, signing certificate, vulnerability scan report, RBAC policy diff, and test coverage report.
  - Store bundle in evidence-bucket with manifest: {release_id, signer, timestamp, s3_path} (manifest is a flattened JSON string in evidence index).

Incident response: evidence-first containment for auth/RBAC incidents:
- Trigger conditions: anomalous role grants, repeated failed MFA for privileged accounts, JIT activation without matching ticket, or evidence of audit log tampering.

- Triage & containment runbook (high level):
  1. Detect: SRE/IR platform rules raise pager. Include initial alert data (actor, action, timestamp, request_id).
  2. Isolate: if a service account is implicated, rotate its keys and isolate affected nodes. If a human actor is implicated, revoke active sessions pending certification.
  3. Evidence capture:
     - Snapshot the audit stream window +/- 2 hours to a write-once evidence bucket.
     - Export affected RBAC policy revisions (full diff) and signed releases.
     - Collect network capture metadata and immutable node disk snapshot index (not raw disks).
  4. Legal & Compliance: engage security-compliance and legal for preservation and escalation.
  5. Postmortem: assemble evidence bundle, include timeline, decisions, and retained artifacts.

- Evidence bundle contents (minimum):
  - Incident manifest (flat fields: incident_id, detection_time, lead, business_impact, evidence_paths).
  - Audit event slice (NDJSON file).
  - RBAC policy history (git patch/diff).
  - JIT activation log and approver identities.
  - Any customer-provided consent or legal hold documents.

Compliance evidence workflow (packaging and handoff):
- Packaging steps (automated where possible):
  1. Generate manifest with canonical fields (release_id | incident_id | deployment_id | evidence_paths | checksum).
  2. Copy artifacts to evidence-bucket with immutability flag and store a signed index entry in the Evidence Ledger (append-only).
  3. Notify legal via configured webhook and create a sealed export (tar + detached signature).
  4. Retain both an encrypted copy in customer-controlled storage (if contract requires) and a Redwood legal copy under restricted access.

- Access and audit: all evidence access requests require a request ticket, approver chain, and an explicit justification. Access events added to the evidence manifest.

Risk, exceptions, and decision log:
- Exception request template (fields): requester, deployment_id, risk_owner, justification, proposed mitigation, timebox (max 90 days), evidence of impact, approvers.
- Exception review cadence: weekly exceptions triage by Platform Security; high-risk exceptions escalated to SOC and Legal.
- Example risk scenarios and mitigations:
  - Risk: Customer requires plaintext prompts for debugging in their on-prem store.
    Mitigation: Use an ephemeral, access-controlled debug session with MFA + timebound retention + audit slice exported to legal archive.
  - Risk: Audit ingestion delays during heavy load.
    Mitigation: Autoscale collector, buffer to disk with signed sequence numbers, and alert when buffer age > 5 minutes.

Operational checklists (quick actions):
- Onboarding a new private deployment:
  1. Confirm residency requirements and contract retention windows.
  2. Provision initial RBAC roles and seed tenant-admins.
  3. Validate audit sink connectivity and test event roundtrip.
  4. Run pre-deploy SDLC gates and sign images.
  5. Provide evidence index link in onboarding packet.

- Quarterly audit & certification:
  - Run entitlement export and compare to expected approval graph.
  - Review immutable evidence buckets and verify retention settings.
  - Produce a certification artifact: signed PDF with summary + attached manifest.

Appendices and examples:
- CLI examples (audit sink health check):
  # Check last ingestion timestamp for deployment
  redwoodctl audit status --deployment priv-deploy-123 --since 1h

- Example manifest (flattened JSON string for index):
  {"manifest_id":"m-20260210-01","deployment_id":"priv-deploy-123","paths":"s3://evidence/priv-deploy-123/m-20260210-01.tar.gz","checksum":"sha256:...","signed_by":"pipeline@redwood.example"}

- Table: Evidence retention decision matrix (text):
  | Artifact | Default retention | Owner | Storage class |
  |---------|------------------:|-------|---------------|
  | Audit NDJSON slices | 1 year | Eng SRE | Immutable hot |
  | RBAC policy history | 7 years | Platform Security | Archive legal |
  | Build artifacts & SBOM | 5 years | Eng Release | Archive |

Change history and references:
- Created by Aisha Patel (Solutions Eng) 2025-04-15.
- Updated 2026-02-10: clarified legal hold steps and added JIT activation audit requirements.
- Key references: private-deploy-reference-architecture, secure-sdlc/signed-release-gates, security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/orchestrated-evidence-rbac-integration-playbook-2026.

Contact and escalation:
- For operational issues: eng-sre@redwood.example
- For RBAC/design questions: platform-security@redwood.example
- For legal or evidence escalation: security-compliance@redwood.example

This playbook is intended to be machine-readable where indicated (NDJSON slices and flattened manifests) and also consumable by auditors. If a specific customer contract imposes stricter controls, those override this baseline.
